findings.title: [P2] Reject path aliases before checking body uniqueness
findings.body: `Path(path)` removes redundant separators and `.` components before the canonical-path check. Consequently, `/dir/body.xml` and `/dir/./body.xml` both pass this check and resolve to the same file. Meanwhile, `execute()` tracks the original strings in `paths`, so these aliases also pass the distinct-path check. A pinned plan can therefore complete with repeated canonical body paths, violating the protocol's eighteen-distinct-path requirement. Compare the supplied string with its canonical spelling before accepting it, and track canonical paths for uniqueness.

overall_explanation: The body input gate does not enforce its documented canonical-path and distinct-path invariants because pathlib normalizes aliases before validation while uniqueness uses raw strings. Review was limited to read-only inspection of the supplied snapshot; no tests or actual invocation were run.
